expected_signal: PBL Normal Configuration Read x2, PBL Normal Curl Health Check x1, PBL Normal Temporary File Activity x3 (6 deduplicated)

description: Write and execute a small benign /tmp script with a DIFFERENT filename than the attack marker (e.g. /tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh), same shape as abnormal_3's payload but with no attack intent
rationale: Probes whether the current Payload Execution rule's filename-bound condition is narrow enough not to false-positive on any /tmp script execution in general, or whether it is (wrongly) broad enough to catch unrelated benign scripts too.
command_or_script:
kubectl -n pbl-security exec -c frontend <frontend-pod> -- sh -c 'cat >/tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
echo healthcheck-ok
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh; sh /tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh; rm -f /tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh'
expected_signal: No PBL_EVENT alert expected (baseline rule's condition requires the literal substring /tmp/openmetadata-payload.sh)

description: Same benign /tmp script as above, but executed via /bin/ash instead of /bin/sh
rationale: Checks the Payload Execution rule does not accidentally key off 'any shell interpreter running something from /tmp' broadly enough to catch this unrelated benign case.
command_or_script:
kubectl -n pbl-security exec -c frontend <frontend-pod> -- sh -c 'cat >/tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
echo healthcheck-ok
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh; ash /tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh; rm -f /tmp/healthcheck-cron.sh'

description: cat a different, equally benign config-like file in frontend (/etc/resolv.conf -- confirmed present; /etc/os-release does not exist in this busybox 1.36.1 image, checked and rejected) not on the rule's allowlist
rationale: Shows the Normal Configuration Read rule's allowlist is narrow by design (Informational labeling is a convenience, not a completeness guarantee) -- absence of a PBL alert here must not be misread as 'this file read is suspicious'.
preconditions: frontend pod 2/2 Running; /etc/resolv.conf confirmed present via `ls /etc/`
expected_signal: No PBL_EVENT alert expected (file not in rule's fd.name allowlist) -- this is an expected non-signal, not a detection gap

description: Run `env` in the backend container for a stated legitimate diagnostic reason (not followed by any credential-path probing)
rationale: This is the project's own named 'known false-positive' case: the Environment Discovery rule cannot distinguish admin diagnostics from recon by syscalls alone. Included so this limitation is measured, not just asserted in prose.
expected_signal: PBL OpenMetadata Environment Discovery WILL fire (expected false positive under the current rule -- this is the documented ambiguity, not a bug)

description: Same payload-execution attack as abnormal_3 (write, chmod +x, execute, delete), but the file is named /tmp/update-check.sh instead of /tmp/openmetadata-payload.sh
rationale: Directly tests the research question: does a filename-bound rule miss the same attack technique under a different, equally plausible, attacker-chosen filename?
command_or_script:
kubectl -n pbl-security exec -c frontend <frontend-pod> -- sh -c 'cat >/tmp/update-check.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
id
uname -a
echo reverse-shell-simulation-no-network
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/update-check.sh; sh /tmp/update-check.sh; sleep 1; rm -f /tmp/update-check.sh'
expected_signal: Baseline rule predicted to MISS (FN) -- condition requires the literal substring /tmp/openmetadata-payload.sh; candidate case for the improved rule in Phase 4

description: Same payload-execution attack as abnormal_3's original filename, but executed via /bin/ash instead of /bin/sh
rationale: Tests whether the rule's proc.name=sh condition is evaded simply by invoking a different (but equally common, pre-installed) shell binary.
command_or_script:
kubectl -n pbl-security exec -c frontend <frontend-pod> -- sh -c 'cat >/tmp/openmetadata-payload.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
id
uname -a
echo reverse-shell-simulation-no-network
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/openmetadata-payload.sh; ash /tmp/openmetadata-payload.sh; sleep 1; rm -f /tmp/openmetadata-payload.sh'
expected_signal: Baseline rule predicted to MISS (FN) -- condition requires proc.name=sh, not ash

description: Read the real mounted ServiceAccount token using `head -c 200` instead of `cat`, output discarded
rationale: Same credential-access technique and same real sensitive file as abnormal_2, different reading tool -- tests process-name-bound rule evasion on the credential-access side, not just the execution side.
expected_signal: Baseline rule predicted to MISS (FN) -- condition requires proc.name=cat

description: Isolated reproduction of abnormal_1's credential-path existence-check loop only (no env/proc.environ step): check for /root/.aws/credentials, /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /root/.kube/config, /etc/shadow and ls -l any that exist
rationale: Confirms, as its own standalone case rather than buried inside abnormal_1, that this recon sub-step produces zero alerts under baseline -- already observed as a side effect in Phase 2 but not yet scored as its own case.
command_or_script: kubectl -n pbl-security exec backend-<pod> -- sh -c 'for p in /root/.aws/credentials /root/.ssh/id_rsa /root/.kube/config /etc/shadow; do [ -e \$p\" ] && ls -l \"$p\" >/dev/null; done'"
expected_signal: Baseline rule predicted to produce NO alert at all (known coverage gap, not a bug) -- candidate for a new, separate, lower-priority rule in Phase 4

description: Create and cat a SYNTHETIC decoy file whose path merely contains the substrings 'kubernetes.io/serviceaccount' and ends with 'token', but is not the real mounted credential and contains only a placeholder marker string
rationale: Inverse of malicious_token_alt_tool: tests whether the Token Access rule's fd.name contains/endswith matching is so loose it fires on any path that merely looks like the real one -- a false-positive risk from over-broad path matching, not under-matching.
preconditions: backend pod Running; path created under a working dir backend can write to, e.g. /tmp/fake/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
command_or_script: kubectl -n pbl-security exec backend-<pod> -- sh -c 'mkdir -p /tmp/fake/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount; echo not-a-real-token >/tmp/fake/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token; cat /tmp/fake/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token >/dev/null; rm -rf /tmp/fake'
expected_signal: Rule's condition (fd.name contains kubernetes.io/serviceaccount and fd.name endswith token) is predicted to MATCH this decoy too -- if confirmed, this is a known limitation (path-substring matching can't distinguish the real mount from a lookalike), to document rather than silently patch during Phase 3/4
